headline: South Korea's main stock index fell about 8% on Thursday as investors hurried to cut their holdings of AI-linked shares.
score_reason: Facts match the headline; figures are mid-session at the time of writing, so the final close may differ.
importance_line: Korean savers and pension holders and foreign investors in the chip makers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix feel it first, then global chip suppliers; the figures are intraday and could change by the close.
summary: Benzinga, in a report carried by AOL, says the KOSPI index fell 7.81% to 5,539.34 in Seoul on Thursday 15 Oct 2026, with SK Hynix down 11.42% and Samsung Electronics down 8.84%, as hot US inflation, Federal Reserve rate-hike bets and doubts over funding the AI build-out hit chip shares; Bloomberg's headline puts the fall at 8%. This continues the slump the Korea Times reported in our 12 Oct 2026 edition, when the index fell 3.65% to 6,384.24.
notes: Bloomberg original returned a bot check (headline only); the facts come from the Benzinga report on AOL, which describes the same Seoul move. Bloomberg is credited in the summary for the 8% figure in its headline only. Follow-up of 1012:C07-02 (Korea Times, KOSPI -3.65% on 12 Oct). Figures are 'at the time of writing', not the closing prices.
